question: Arjun starts his journey on Monday. He completes it in 365 days. On which day will Arjun reach his destination?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Tuesday.

GIVEN

• Start day = Monday. Duration = 365 days.

SOLUTION

• Odd days = 365 ÷ 7 = 52 weeks and 1 odd day (365 = 52 × 7 + 1).

• The day after 365 days = Monday + 1 day = Tuesday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• An ordinary year (365 days) shifts the weekday by 1: the same date next year falls on the next weekday. A leap year (366 days) shifts it by 2.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Friday) is wrong: it needs 4 odd days, but there is only 1.

• Option 2 (Sunday) is wrong: it needs 6 odd days (or −1), but there is 1. (The PDF shows this option as a wrong selection.)

• Option 4 (Wednesday) is wrong: it needs 2 odd days, but there is only 1.

• Remember: 7 odd days = 0 (a complete week); ordinary year = 1 odd day, leap year = 2 odd days.

question: In the following question, a matrix of numbers is given. These numbers follow a certain pattern either row-wise or column-wise. Identify this pattern and choose the missing number accordingly.
solution_text:

SOLUTION

• Row 2: 6² + 8² = 36 + 64 = 100 ✓. Row 3: 9² + 12² = 81 + 144 = 225 ✓.

• Row 1: ?² + 5² = 74, so ?² = 74 − 25 = 49 and ? = 7.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

NOTE

• Option 1 (3) is wrong: 3² + 5² = 34, not 74.

• Option 2 (11) is wrong: 11² + 5² = 146, not 74.

• Option 4 (14) is wrong: 14² + 5² = 221, not 74.

question: In a non-leap year, if 1 January is Wednesday, how many Mondays will occur in February and March together?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 9.

GIVEN

• Non-leap year (February has 28 days); 1 January = Wednesday.

SOLUTION

• January has 31 days = 4 weeks + 3 odd days, so 1 February = Wednesday + 3 = Saturday.

• February (28 days) has exactly 4 weeks, so each weekday occurs exactly 4 times: 4 Mondays (3, 10, 17, 24 February).

• 1 March = Saturday again (28 days = 0 odd days). March has 31 days, and the first three weekdays (Saturday, Sunday, Monday) occur 5 times, so Monday occurs 5 times (3, 10, 17, 24, 31 March).

• Total = 4 + 5 = 9.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• A 31-day month has 3 extra days: the weekdays of the 1st, 2nd and 3rd of the month occur 5 times. March 1 is a Saturday, so Saturday, Sunday and Monday occur 5 times.

NOTE

• Option 1 (8) is wrong: it counts only 4 Mondays in each month, ignoring the fifth Monday on 31 March.

• Option 3 (10) is wrong: it would need 5 Mondays in February as well, but February has only 28 days (4 Mondays).

• Option 4 (11) is wrong: it would need more Mondays than the 4 in February and 5 in March.

• Odd-day count: 31 days = 3 odd days; 30 days = 2 odd days; 28 days = 0 odd days; 29 days = 1 odd day.

question: If A = +, B = ÷, C = ×, D = −, find: (40 A 20) B 5 C 2 D 6 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 18.

• Replace the letters with the signs: (40 + 20) ÷ 5 × 2 − 6.

• Bracket first: 60 ÷ 5 × 2 − 6.

• Then ÷ and × from left to right: 60 ÷ 5 = 12; 12 × 2 = 24.

• Finally 24 − 6 = 18.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Substitute, then apply BODMAS: bracket → division → multiplication → subtraction.

NOTE

• Option 2 (14) is wrong: it does not equal 24 − 6.

• Option 4 (22) is wrong: it does not equal 24 − 6 = 18.

• BODMAS: Brackets, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction (× and ÷ are done from left to right).

question: If the time is 4:20, what will be the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of the clock?
solution_text:

• Time = 4:20 (H = 4, M = 20).

SOLUTION

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

NOTE

• Option 2 (18°) is wrong: it does not equal |120 − 110| = 10°.

• Option 4 (26°) is wrong: it does not equal |120 − 110| = 10°.

• Formula: angle = |30H − 5.5M|; if the result is more than 180°, subtract it from 360°.

question:
Mrs. Carson and her three friends tried to remember the taxi number after she accidentally left her bag inside. Each of them recalled it differently as JXK12L, JXM12L, JYK12L, and JXK92L. During discussion, they concluded that all four of them were correct about the first letter, three of them agreed on the last three characters, three believed that the second letter was X, and three believed that the third letter was K.

 

Based on this information, which is the most likely correct taxi number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. JXK12L.

GIVEN

• Four recalled numbers: JXK12L, JXM12L, JYK12L, JXK92L. All four agree on the first letter (J); three agree on the last three characters; three believe the second letter is X; three believe the third letter is K.

SOLUTION

• First letter: J (all four) — all options start with J.

• Last three characters: "12L" appears in three recollections (JXK12L, JXM12L, JYK12L), and "92L" in only one, so the last three characters are 12L.

• Second letter: X appears in three (JXK12L, JXM12L, JXK92L), Y in one, so it is X.

• Third letter: K appears in three (JXK12L, JYK12L, JXK92L), M in one, so it is K.

• The correct taxi number is JXK12L.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Take the "majority" for each position: J, X, K, 1, 2, L → JXK12L.

NOTE

• Option 2 (JYK12L) is wrong: it has Y as the second letter, but three people said X.

• Option 3 (JXM12L) is wrong: it has M as the third letter, but three people said K.

• Option 4 (JXK92L) is wrong: its last three characters are 92L, but three people agreed on 12L.

• Method: check each position separately and select the value in the majority.

question:
Looking at a boy, Anu says: "He is the son of my grandfather's only son."

 

Anu is the boy's _.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Sister.

GIVEN

• Anu says: "He is the son of my grandfather's only son."

SOLUTION

• Anu's grandfather's only son = Anu's father.

• So the boy is the son of Anu's father, which makes the boy Anu's brother.

• Anu is therefore the boy's sister (the options use the female relation, so Anu is a girl).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Grandfather's only son = father. "Son of my father" = my brother. So the speaker is his sibling (sister, since the answer must be female).

NOTE

• Option 2 (Mother) is wrong: the boy is the son of Anu's father, so the boy is Anu's brother, not her son.

• Option 3 (Aunt) is wrong: an aunt would be the sister of the boy's parent, but Anu and the boy have the same father.

• Option 4 (Cousin) is wrong: cousins have different parents who are siblings; here they have the same father.

• Relation tips: grandfather's only son = father (if the speaker's father is meant) or uncle (if it is another person's); "only son" removes the uncle possibility.

question: If (2,4,6) → 12 and (3,6,9) → 27, then find (4,8,12) → ?

question:
Classify Inference II from the passage using the standard scale: Definitely True (DT), Probably True (PT), Probably False (PF), or Definitely False (DF).

 

Passage: A study across 40 countries found that nations where citizens averaged more than 7 hours of sleep per night had significantly lower rates of lifestyle diseases such as type 2 diabetes and hypertension compared to nations where average sleep was below 6 hours.

 

Inference I: Sleeping more than 7 hours is the only factor preventing lifestyle diseases.

Inference II: Adequate sleep may be associated with lower prevalence of certain lifestyle diseases.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. DT.

GIVEN

• Passage: countries with more than 7 hours of average sleep had significantly lower rates of lifestyle diseases than countries with less than 6 hours.

• Inference II: Adequate sleep may be associated with lower prevalence of certain lifestyle diseases.

SOLUTION

• The passage directly reports a link (an association) between adequate sleep and lower rates of diabetes and hypertension.

• Inference II only says "may be associated", which is exactly what the passage supports, and does not claim a cause. So it is Definitely True (DT).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Check whether the inference goes beyond the passage. Words like "may be associated" are weak and fit the data; words like "only" or "always" (as in Inference I) are strong and usually make an inference false.

NOTE

• Option 2 (PT) is wrong: the inference is directly stated in the passage, so it is not just "probably" true.

• Option 3 (DF) is wrong: the passage supports the inference, so it cannot be definitely false.

• Option 4 (PF) is wrong: the passage supports the inference, so it cannot be probably false.

• Scale: DT (follows from the facts), PT (likely but not certain), PF (unlikely), DF (contradicted by the facts).

question: At what time between 5 and 6 o’clock will the angle between the hands be 3 times the smaller angle at 5:00?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 5 : 10 10/11 & 5 : 43 7/11.

GIVEN

• Find the times between 5 and 6 o'clock at which the angle between the hands equals the angle given in the question.

SOLUTION

• At m minutes past 5, the angle between the hands = |150 + 0.5m − 6m| = |150 − 5.5m|.

• Using the key given in the PDF, the angle required is 90° (the right angle, 3 × 30°).

• Case 1: 150 − 5.5m = 90 → m = 60 ÷ 5.5 = 120/11 = 10 10/11 minutes, so the time is 5 : 10 10/11.

• Case 2: 5.5m − 150 = 90 → m = 240 ÷ 5.5 = 480/11 = 43 7/11 minutes, so the time is 5 : 43 7/11.

• Answer: 5 : 10 10/11 & 5 : 43 7/11.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Time between H and (H + 1) at which the hands make an angle θ: m = (30H ± θ) ÷ 5.5 = (150 ± 90) × 2/11 → 120/11 and 480/11.

NOTE

• Option 2 (5:10 & 5:43) is wrong: these are only rounded values, and at exactly 5:10 and 5:43 the angle is about 95° and 86.5°, not 90°.

• Option 3 (5 : 7 10/11 & 5 : 10 7/11) is wrong: at these times the angle is about 106.5° and 91.5°, not 90°.

• Option 4 (5 : 10 7/11 & 5 : 43 10/11) is wrong: the minute values are interchanged between the two fractions, and at these times the angle is not 90°. (The PDF shows this option as a wrong selection.)

• Formula: angle between the hands at H hours and M minutes = |30H − 5.5M|.

FLAG

• The smaller angle between the hands at 5:00 is 150°, and 3 times 150° (450°) is not possible, so the wording of the question is unclear. The PDF key (Option 1) corresponds to the times at which the hands are at 90° to each other, and it is kept unchanged here; please confirm.

question: During the Delhi Sultanate period, the Lodi dynasty introduced the architectural concept of the 'double dome'. What was the primary structural purpose behind this innovation?

option_2: To create an acoustic chamber for the muezzin.

question: What is the fundamental reason for the regular occurrence of day and night on Earth as it experiences alternating periods of light and darkness?
option_2: Rotation on its own axis daily
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rotation on its own axis daily.

 

ANSWER

 

• Rotation on its own axis daily.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

EXPLANATION

 

• The Earth rotates on its axis from west to east once in about 24 hours. At any time, the half facing the Sun has day and the other half has night, so rotation causes the alternation of day and night.

 

WHY THE OTHERS ARE WRONG

 

• Option 1 (Revolution around the Sun annually) is wrong: revolution (365¼ days) causes the seasons and the change in length of day and night, not the daily cycle.

 

• Option 3 (Gravitational pull of Moon) is wrong: the Moon's pull causes tides.

 

• Option 4 (Solar radiation fluctuations) is wrong: the Sun's output is almost steady and does not produce the daily cycle.

 

EXTRA FACTS

 

• Rotation: day and night; time difference between longitudes (4 minutes per degree). Revolution: seasons, change in day length. Tilt of the axis (23½°) with revolution gives the seasons.

question: Which phenomenon accounts for the observed shift in the positions of stars in the night sky when viewed from Earth at different times?
solution_text:

EXTRA FACTS

 

• The Pole Star (Polaris) seems fixed as it lies almost on the Earth's axis of rotation, and other stars seem to circle around it.

question: In a situation where Union and State laws conflict on a Concurrent List subject and the state law has Presidential assent, which principle determines validity of the law?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Doctrine of Repugnancy.

 

ANSWER

 

• Doctrine of Repugnancy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

EXPLANATION

 

• Article 254 deals with a conflict between Union and State laws on a Concurrent List subject. Under Article 254(1) the Union law prevails; under Article 254(2), a State law that has received the President's assent prevails in that State, though Parliament can still override it later by law. This is decided through the doctrine of repugnancy.

 

WHY THE OTHERS ARE WRONG

 

• Option 1 (Doctrine of Eclipse) is wrong: it applies to pre-Constitution laws that violate Fundamental Rights, which become dormant (eclipsed) and not void.

 

• Option 3 (Doctrine of Severability) is wrong: it separates the invalid part of a law from the valid part (Article 13).

 

• Option 4 (Doctrine of Pith and Substance) is wrong: it finds the true nature of a law to decide which List it falls under, and not how a clash on a Concurrent subject is settled.

 

EXTRA FACTS

 

• Article 246: three Lists (Union, State, Concurrent). The Concurrent List has 52 subjects. Residuary powers lie with Parliament (Article 248).

question: Which two international financial institutions did India approach for a loan to manage the 1991 economic crisis?

question: Which of the following processes is correctly matched with the organisms/cells that perform it?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Anaerobic respiration – Yeast.

 

ANSWER

 

• Anaerobic respiration – Yeast.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

EXPLANATION

 

• Yeast can respire without oxygen: it breaks down glucose to ethanol and carbon dioxide (alcoholic fermentation), which is its anaerobic mode of getting energy. So "Anaerobic respiration – Yeast" is the only correct pair.

 

WHY THE OTHERS ARE WRONG

 

• Option 1 (Lactic acid fermentation – Yeast) is wrong: lactic acid fermentation occurs in muscle cells and in bacteria like Lactobacillus; yeast makes ethanol.

 

• Option 2 (Alcoholic fermentation – Human muscle cells) is wrong: human muscle cells make lactic acid when oxygen is short, not ethanol.

 

• Option 3 (Aerobic respiration – Obligate anaerobes) is wrong: obligate anaerobes cannot use oxygen and die in it.

 

EXTRA FACTS

question: Why are aggregate statistics (like death rate) considered social phenomena rather than just individual data?
option_3: They reflect patterns influenced by society.

question: Simplify:18 − [5 − {6 + 2(7 − 8̅ ̅−̅ ̅5̅)}].
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 27.

GIVEN

• Expression: 18 − [5 − {6 + 2(7 − (8̅ ̅−̅ ̅5̅))}] (the bar covers 8 − 5).

SOLUTION

• Bar first: 8 − 5 = 3

• Bracket: 7 − 3 = 4

• 2 × 4 = 8

• Curly bracket: 6 + 8 = 14

• Square bracket: 5 − 14 = −9

• Result: 18 − (−9) = 18 + 9 = 27

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Use BODMAS and open the brackets from the inside out: vinculum (bar) → ( ) → { } → [ ]. Remember that minus before a negative number becomes plus.

NOTE

• Option 1 (15), Option 3 (18) and Option 4 (32) are wrong: 15 and 32 come from sign mistakes, and 18 comes from leaving out the final bracket value (18 − 0).

question: The average marks obtained by Madhu in 4 subjects is 64. If she scored 69 marks in the fifth subject, then find the new average of marks obtained by her in all 5 subjects.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 65.

GIVEN

• Average of 4 subjects = 64; fifth subject = 69.

SOLUTION

• Total of 4 subjects = 64 × 4 = 256

• Total of 5 subjects = 256 + 69 = 325

• New average = 325 ÷ 5 = 65

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• New average = old average + (new score − old average) ÷ 5 = 64 + (69 − 64) ÷ 5 = 64 + 1 = 65.

NOTE

• Option 1 (68), Option 2 (88) and Option 4 (78) are wrong: they do not match 325 ÷ 5; for example, 68 is not the result of 64 + 4 from the wrong division, and 88 and 78 are far above any average that can come from these marks.

question: The average of 100 numbers is 44. If four new numbers are included, the average of the entire set becomes 50. Find the average of the four newly added numbers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 200.

GIVEN

• 100 numbers with average 44; after adding 4 numbers, 104 numbers with average 50.

SOLUTION

• Sum of 100 numbers = 44 × 100 = 4400

• Sum of 104 numbers = 50 × 104 = 5200

• Sum of the 4 new numbers = 5200 − 4400 = 800

• Average of the 4 new numbers = 800 ÷ 4 = 200

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Rise of 6 in the average of 104 numbers: 6 × 104 = 624 extra; the new numbers must also cover 44 each: 4 × 44 = 176. Total = 624 + 176 = 800, so average = 200.

NOTE

• Option 1 (150), Option 2 (180) and Option 4 (220) are wrong: none of them gives a total of 800 for four numbers (they give 600, 720 and 880).

question: 7 workers take 20 weeks to build a house. How long would it take 10 workers to build the same house?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 14 weeks.

GIVEN

• 7 workers → 20 weeks; 10 workers → ?

SOLUTION

• Work is fixed, so workers × time is constant (inverse proportion).

• Total work = 7 × 20 = 140 worker-weeks

• Time for 10 workers = 140 ÷ 10 = 14 weeks

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• More workers means less time: M₁ × D₁ = M₂ × D₂ → 7 × 20 = 10 × D₂ → D₂ = 14.

NOTE

• Option 1 (7 weeks), Option 2 (10 weeks) and Option 3 (12 weeks) are wrong: 10 workers × 7, 10 or 12 weeks gives 70, 100 or 120 worker-weeks, not 140.

question: Simplify using BODMAS : [(60 ÷ 12) + (19 - 12)] × 2 - 16 + 20
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 28.

GIVEN

• Expression: [(60 ÷ 12) + (19 − 12)] × 2 − 16 + 20

SOLUTION

• Brackets: 60 ÷ 12 = 5 and 19 − 12 = 7

• [5 + 7] = 12

• Multiplication: 12 × 2 = 24

• Then left to right: 24 − 16 + 20 = 8 + 20 = 28

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• BODMAS: Brackets, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction. After the brackets and the multiplication, + and − are done left to right.

NOTE

• Option 2 (−12) is wrong: it comes from 24 − (16 + 20) = −12, grouping the last two terms. Option 3 (−148) and Option 4 (60) are wrong: they come from wrong order of operations, such as multiplying before adding the bracket.

question: Two adjacent angles form a linear pair. If one angle is 38°, then the other angle is:

The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 142°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

• Linear pair: sum = 180°. Supplement of 38° = 142° (just subtract from 180).

NOTE

• Option 1 (138°) and Option 3 (146°) are wrong: 38° + 138° = 176° and 38° + 146° = 184°, not 180°. Option 4 (38°) is wrong: it is the given angle itself, and 38° + 38° = 76°.

question: If two adjacent angles are (1X + 3)° and (2X + 15)° and they form a linear pair, then the smaller angle is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 57°.

GIVEN

• Angles (X + 3)° and (2X + 15)° form a linear pair.

SOLUTION

• (X + 3) + (2X + 15) = 180

• 3X + 18 = 180 → 3X = 162 → X = 54

• First angle = 54 + 3 = 57°

• Second angle = 2 × 54 + 15 = 123°

• Smaller angle = 57°

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Add the angles, make 180, solve X, then put X back in both angles and compare the two.

NOTE

• Option 1 (54°) is wrong: it is the value of X, not an angle. Option 3 (123°) is wrong: it is the larger angle. Option 4 (60°) is wrong: it does not match either angle.

question: A shopkeeper marks a toy at Rs. 400 and gives a discount of Rs. 60. What is the discount percent?

question: A jacket is marked at Rs. 2500. Two successive discounts of 10% and 20% are offered. What is the final selling price?

question: A sum of ₹460 grows to ₹640 in 6 years under simple interest. Find the total amount it would reach in just 2 years at the same annual interest rate.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. ₹520.

GIVEN

• Principal = ₹460; amount after 6 years = ₹640; find the amount after 2 years.

SOLUTION

• Interest in 6 years = 640 − 460 = ₹180

• Interest per year = 180 ÷ 6 = ₹30

• Interest in 2 years = 30 × 2 = ₹60

• Amount after 2 years = 460 + 60 = ₹520

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• In simple interest the interest is the same every year, so 2 years is one-third of 6 years: 180 ÷ 3 = 60; 460 + 60 = 520.

NOTE

• Option 1 (₹480), Option 2 (₹500) and Option 4 (₹540) are wrong: they would need interest of ₹20, ₹40 and ₹80 in 2 years, but the interest is ₹60.

question: The number of students in a school increased from 800 to 920 in one year. By what percent did it increase?
solution_text:

SOLUTION

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

question: A bus travels 240 km at a speed of 60 km/h. How much time does it take?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 4 hours.

GIVEN

• Distance = 240 km; speed = 60 km/h.

SOLUTION

• Time = Distance ÷ Speed = 240 ÷ 60 = 4 hours

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

• Distance = Speed × Time, so Time = Distance ÷ Speed. Cancel the zeros: 24 ÷ 6 = 4.

question: A boat travels 36 km downstream in 3 hours and the same distance upstream in 4.5 hours. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 10 km/h.

GIVEN

• Distance = 36 km; downstream time = 3 h; upstream time = 4.5 h.

SOLUTION

• Speed in still water = (12 + 8) ÷ 2 = 10 km/h

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

• Option 1 (8 km/h) is wrong: it is the upstream speed. Option 2 (9 km/h) is wrong: it does not match the average of 12 and 8. Option 4 (12 km/h) is wrong: it is the downstream speed.

question: A and B together can complete a job in 4 days. What part of the job remains after they work together for 1 day?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. ¾.

GIVEN

• A and B together finish the job in 4 days.

SOLUTION

• Work done in 1 day = ¼ of the job

• Work remaining = 1 − ¼ = ¾

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• If the whole job takes n days, 1 day's work is 1/n, and the rest is (n − 1)/n = 3/4.

• Option 1 (¼) is wrong: it is the part completed in 1 day. Option 2 (½) is wrong: it would be the remainder after 2 days. Option 4 (⅔) is wrong: it would be the remainder if the job took 3 days.

question: A contractor planned to finish a work in 24 days with 15 workers. After 8 days, 5 more workers joined and all workers worked at the same rate. In how many total days was the work finished?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 20 days.

GIVEN

• Plan: 24 days with 15 workers; after 8 days, 5 more workers join (total 20).

SOLUTION

• Total work = 15 × 24 = 360 worker-days

• Work done in 8 days = 15 × 8 = 120

• Work left = 360 − 120 = 240

• Time with 20 workers = 240 ÷ 20 = 12 days

• Total days = 8 + 12 = 20 days

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Remaining days at the old strength = 16; with 20 workers instead of 15: 16 × 15/20 = 12. Total = 8 + 12 = 20.

NOTE

• Option 1 (18 days), Option 3 (21 days) and Option 4 (22 days) are wrong: they do not satisfy 8 days of 15 workers plus the remaining work done by 20 workers.

question: Which statement is always true?
option_1: Every whole number is a natural number
option_2: Every irrational number is a real number
option_4: Every integer is a whole number
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Every irrational number is a real number.

GIVEN

• Number systems: N (natural) ⊂ W (whole) ⊂ Z (integers) ⊂ Q (rational) ⊂ R (real); irrational numbers are real numbers that are not rational.

SOLUTION

• Real numbers = rational numbers + irrational numbers, so every irrational number is a real number. Option 2 is always true.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Check each statement with one counter-example; if one exists, the statement is false.

NOTE

• Option 1 is wrong: 0 is a whole number but not a natural number.

• Option 3 is wrong: √2 and π are real but not rational.

• Option 4 is wrong: −3 is an integer but not a whole number.

question: Which one of the following sets is empty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Integers ∩ Irrational numbers.

GIVEN

• Four intersections of number sets.

SOLUTION

• Integers are rational numbers, and no number is both rational and irrational. So Integers ∩ Irrational numbers = ∅ (empty). Option 2.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Rational and irrational numbers have nothing in common, so any subset of rationals (N, W, Z) meets irrationals in the empty set.

NOTE

• Option 1 is wrong: 2, 4, 6 … are both natural and even. Option 3 is wrong: all whole numbers are rational, so the intersection is the set of whole numbers. Option 4 is wrong: all irrational numbers are real, so the intersection is the irrational numbers.

question: The radius of a cone is 7 cm and its slant height is 25 cm. Find the height of the cone.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 24 cm.

GIVEN

• Radius r = 7 cm; slant height l = 25 cm.

SOLUTION

• l² = r² + h², so h² = l² − r² = 25² − 7² = 625 − 49 = 576

• h = √576 = 24 cm

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• (7, 24, 25) is a Pythagorean triplet; learn (3,4,5), (5,12,13), (8,15,17), (7,24,25), (9,40,41).

NOTE

• Option 2 (26 cm) is wrong: it is greater than the slant height, which is impossible, as the height of a cone is always less than its slant height. Option 3 (22 cm) and Option 4 (20 cm) are wrong: 22² + 7² = 533 and 20² + 7² = 449, neither equals 625.

question: Express the repeating decimal 0.41666... as a simple fraction in its lowest terms.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. ⁵⁄₁₂.

GIVEN

• 0.41666… = 0.41 followed by 6 repeating.

SOLUTION

• Let x = 0.41666…

• 100x = 41.666… and 1000x = 416.666…

• Subtract: 900x = 375 → x = 375/900 = 5/12

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• For 0.ab c̄ type: (number without the bar − number before the repeating part) ÷ (9 for each repeating digit, 0 for each non-repeating digit) = (416 − 41)/900 = 375/900 = 5/12.

NOTE

• Option 1 (6/18 = 1/3 = 0.333…) is wrong. Option 3 (3/18 = 1/6 = 0.1666…) is wrong. Option 4 (7/15 = 0.4666…) is wrong. Only 5/12 gives 0.41666….

question:
Solve the following expression and write your final answer as a simplified mixed fraction:

(4.875 − 2⅚) ÷ 0.175
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 11⅔.

GIVEN

• (4.875 − 2⅚) ÷ 0.175

SOLUTION

• 4.875 = 4⅞ = 39/8, and 2⅚ = 17/6

• 39/8 − 17/6 = (117 − 68)/24 = 49/24

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

• Convert decimals to fractions with the same LCM, then dividing by a fraction means multiplying by its reciprocal; cancel 49 with 7 first.

NOTE

• Option 1 (13¾), Option 2 (11½) and Option 3 (12¾) are wrong: 13¾ = 55/4, 11½ = 23/2 and 12¾ = 51/4, none of which equals 35/3.

question: A train moving at 72 km/h crosses a bridge in 30 seconds. How much time will it take to cross the same bridge if the speed becomes 90 km/h?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 24 seconds.

GIVEN

• Speed 72 km/h → 30 s; new speed 90 km/h; same bridge.

SOLUTION

• The distance to cover is the same, so time is inversely proportional to speed.

• New time = 30 × 72/90 = 30 × 4/5 = 24 seconds

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Time ∝ 1/speed: ratio of speeds 72 : 90 = 4 : 5, so ratio of times = 5 : 4, which gives 30 × 4/5 = 24.

NOTE

• Option 1 (20 s), Option 2 (22 s) and Option 4 (25 s) are wrong: they do not follow the inverse ratio 5 : 4.

question: A, B, and C invest money in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5. A invests for 12 months, B for 8 months, and C for 6 months. What is the ratio of their profits?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 4 : 4 : 5.

GIVEN

• Investments 2 : 3 : 5; time 12, 8 and 6 months.

SOLUTION

• Profit ratio = investment × time

• A : B : C = 2 × 12 : 3 × 8 : 5 × 6 = 24 : 24 : 30

• Divide by 6: 4 : 4 : 5

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

• Partnership: Profit ∝ Capital × Time. Always multiply each pair, then reduce.

• Option 1 (2 : 1 : 5), Option 2 (2 : 4 : 5) and Option 4 (3 : 1 : 5) are wrong: they do not reduce from 24 : 24 : 30.

question: A 6 cm × 6 cm square has a 2 cm × 2 cm square cut out from one corner. Find the perimeter of the resulting figure.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 24 cm.

GIVEN

• Square of side 6 cm; a 2 cm × 2 cm square is removed from one corner.

SOLUTION

• Perimeter of the 6 cm square = 4 × 6 = 24 cm

• Cutting a square out of a corner removes 2 cm from each of two sides (total 4 cm) and adds two new edges of 2 cm each (total 4 cm).

• New perimeter = 24 − 4 + 4 = 24 cm

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Cutting a rectangle from a corner never changes the perimeter: the outline still has the same total horizontal and vertical lengths (6 + 6 across and 6 + 6 up and down).

NOTE

• Option 2 (20 cm), Option 3 (18 cm) and Option 4 (14 cm) are wrong: they come from wrongly subtracting the cut edges (for example, 24 − 4 = 20) without adding the two new edges.

question: A rectangular parallelepiped has a length of 8 cm, a width of 5 cm, and a height of 3 cm. What is its total surface area?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 158 cm².

GIVEN

• Cuboid with l = 8 cm, b = 5 cm, h = 3 cm.

SOLUTION

• Total surface area = 2(lb + bh + hl)

• = 2(8 × 5 + 5 × 3 + 3 × 8) = 2(40 + 15 + 24) = 2 × 79 = 158 cm²

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Add the three face-pair areas first (40 + 15 + 24 = 79) and then double it. Volume = lbh = 120 cm³; space diagonal = √(l² + b² + h²).

NOTE

• Option 1 (168 cm²), Option 3 (128 cm²) and Option 4 (138 cm²) are wrong: they come from arithmetic slips; for example, 138 comes from leaving out the face pair of 8 × 3 and 128 is not 2 × any valid sum.

question:
In the following question, four sentences from a paragraph are provided. The sentences are jumbled and labeled A, B, C and D. Rearrange these sentences into the correct sequence to form a logically and grammatically coherent paragraph. From the given alternatives, select the option that represents the correct sequence.

 

A. The first set of rules were formulated in Pune, in India in 1901.

B. Badminton is a game which is played by men, women (Singles/Doubles) and both men and women ( Mixed Doubles) together.

C. These rules were gradually adopted by other nations.

D. It can be played by persons of all ages.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. BDAC.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Correct order: B → D → A → C (BDAC).

 

• B introduces the topic: Badminton and who plays it. D says "It" (badminton) can be played by all ages, so it follows B. A moves to the history: "The first set of rules" (1901, Pune). C says "These rules" were adopted by other nations, so it must come right after A.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (ADBC) is wrong: it starts with "The first set of rules" before the game is named, and "It" in D would have no clear noun.

 

• Option 2 (CDBA) is wrong: C begins with "These rules", which has no earlier mention of rules.

 

• Option 4 (CADB) is wrong: C begins with "These rules" before any rules are introduced.

 

NOTE

 

• Para-jumble tips: find the opening sentence that introduces the topic (no pronoun like "It" or "These"); then link pronouns and linkers (It, These, This) to the noun just before them.
